Useful guidance needs clear boundaries

  • Every reading explains where it came from and how fresh it is.
  • Children use aliases. No date of birth or diagnosis is needed.
  • Channel consent, quiet hours and daily limits control notifications.
  • A school adult publishes the instruction. A receipt records review.
  • Indoor conditions are unknown unless measured.

Honest boundaries

Does this measure air at my school gate?

Regional model estimates describe a wider area. They do not prove conditions at the school gate. The workspace shows sources and observation times; suitable local sensors need installation and assessment.

Is the example plan a real school instruction?

No. The landing page example is an illustration. The local cloud preview uses labelled fictional data and sends no messages. In a configured school workspace, follow the school’s actual published instruction.

What information do children need to share?

This home page and learning question need no child details. School profiles use aliases, age groups and optional caution preferences. A school administrator controls membership and role access.

How does AWS fit?

The project includes a cloud implementation for Cognito, DynamoDB and Lambda, plus a working local preview. Cloud deployment has not been verified. The original local API uses Powertools for AWS Lambda, an AWS open-source project.

The implementation behind the plan

The local preview uses fictional inputs and MemoryStore. The actual Powertools Lambda handler runs at the local engine demonstration. Cognito, Lambda, DynamoDB and SQS are implemented in the separate cloud template; deployment is unverified. No external messages are sent.
